settings.config.sessions.intro: These rules decide when an end user's session ends. They are checked on every request the user makes.
settings.config.sessions.lifetime.title: Session lifetime
settings.config.sessions.lifetime.intro: A session ends when it is unused for too long or reaches its maximum age.
settings.config.sessions.inactivity.hint: A session unused for this long becomes idle and ends as 'Timed out' on its next request or at the next idle check. Also decides who counts as online.
settings.config.sessions.maxAge.label: Maximum session age
settings.config.sessions.maxAge.hint: Counted from sign-in, regardless of activity. Applied on the session's next request; until then the session can still show as active or idle.
settings.config.sessions.lastSeen.label: Update "Last active" at most every
settings.config.sessions.lastSeen.hint: Lower values make 'Last active' and idle detection more precise but write to the database more often.
settings.config.sessions.lastSeen.warnin: This is not clearly shorter than the inactivity timeout, so sessions in use can show as idle.
settings.config.sessions.idleCheck.label: Run idle check every
settings.config.sessions.idleCheck.hint: The idle check ends idle sessions as 'Timed out'. It deletes nothing. It also runs once at server start.
settings.config.sessions.idleMethod.hint: Direct SQL is faster but skips lifecycle hooks. Ignored when Strapi's refresh-token mode is on.
settings.config.token.title: Token check
settings.config.token.intro: Decides what happens to a token that Session Manager has no record for. Ended, expired and revoked sessions and blocked users are always rejected.
settings.config.token.check.label: Strict token check
settings.config.token.check.hint: Rejects tokens without a session record and requests where the check itself fails.
settings.config.token.relaxedWarning: Tokens without a session record are accepted. If the check itself fails, up to 10 requests per minute are still allowed.
settings.config.token.grace.label: Grace period after sign-in
settings.config.token.grace.hint: Accepts a new token for a few seconds while its session record is being created. Only for tokens without a session record. Not used when Strapi's refresh-token mode (jwtManagement: 'refresh') is on.
settings.config.token.key.label: Token encryption key
settings.config.token.key.hint: Session Manager encrypts stored tokens with this environment variable. Not needed in Strapi's refresh-token mode. Nothing is saved here.
settings.config.token.key.placeholder: Select Generate key to create a key.
settings.config.token.key.copied: Copied. Add it to your server environment and restart Strapi.
settings.config.rejected.title: When a session is rejected
settings.config.rejected.intro: What your app receives when a request uses an ended session.
settings.config.rejected.body: The response is 401 with the header {header} and the reason: {reasons}.
settings.config.rejected.reason.manual: Ended from the Strapi admin, or by the user from another of their devices.
settings.config.rejected.reason.idle: Not used for longer than the inactivity timeout.
settings.config.rejected.reason.blocked: Ended because the user account was blocked.
settings.config.loginProtection.intro: These rules check new sign-ins before they succeed. Existing sessions are not affected, and refused sign-ins are not recorded.
settings.config.failed.title: Failed sign-ins
settings.config.failed.intro: Slows down password guessing from one IP address.
settings.config.failed.lockout.label: Temporary IP lockout after
settings.config.failed.lockout.hint: A whole number from 0 to 100. 0 turns the lockout off.
settings.config.failed.lockout.off: The temporary IP lockout is off. Failed sign-ins are not limited.
settings.config.failed.lockout.preview: After {count, plural, one {# failed sign-in} other {# failed sign-ins}} from one IP address within 15 minutes, that address is refused for 15 minutes. User accounts are not blocked. Counted per server process.
settings.config.clientIp.title: Client IP address
settings.config.clientIp.intro: All IP-based rules depend on reading the real client address.
settings.config.clientIp.trustProxy.hint: Turn on only behind a proxy you control. Affects the recorded IP address, the IP lockout and location lookups.
settings.config.suspicious.title: Suspicious sign-ins
settings.config.suspicious.intro: Refuses new sign-ins that look risky.
settings.config.suspicious.reject.label: Reject suspicious sign-ins
settings.config.suspicious.reject.hint: Refuses sign-ins from VPN, proxy or known threat addresses and, with security scoring on, scores below 50.
settings.config.suspicious.reject.localN: The local database has no VPN, proxy or threat data and always scores 100, so only failed lookups can be refused.
settings.config.suspicious.failureMode.l: If the location cannot be determined
settings.config.suspicious.failureMode.h: Automatic rejects only when 'Reject suspicious sign-ins' is on. A rejected sign-in gets 'Login temporarily unavailable'. With 'Reject sign-in', the Automatic provider no longer falls back to ipapi.co.
settings.config.countries.title: Country rules
settings.config.countries.intro: Allow or reject new sign-ins by the country of the IP address.
settings.config.countries.enable.label: Use country rules
settings.config.countries.mode.label: Mode
settings.config.countries.switch.title: Switch to {mode}?
settings.config.countries.switch.body: The current list of {count, plural, one {# country} other {# countries}} is cleared when you save.
settings.config.countries.list.label: Countries
settings.config.countries.list.hint: With 'Allow only listed countries', an empty list allows every country.
settings.config.refused.title: Why sign-ins are refused
settings.config.refused.rule.cause: Country rule, or suspicious address / low score
settings.config.refused.unavailable.caus: Location could not be determined and the rule says reject
settings.config.refused.noLog: Session Manager keeps no log of refused sign-ins.
settings.config.locationData.intro: Location and risk data power country rules, suspicious-sign-in checks and alerts. Turn the lookup off to stop all location processing.
settings.config.locationData.clientIpLin: The client IP address source is set under Login protection › Client IP address.
settings.config.lookup.title: IP location lookup
settings.config.lookup.enable.label: IP location lookup
settings.config.lookup.enable.hint: Looks up country and city at every sign-in and for listed sessions without a location.
settings.config.lookup.enable.privacy: With the Automatic or ipapi.co provider, IP addresses can be sent to ipapi.co.
settings.config.lookup.scoring.label: Security scoring
settings.config.lookup.scoring.hint: Applies the score thresholds: below 70 triggers a suspicious-sign-in email, below 50 a rejection if enabled. Local database results always score 100.
settings.config.provider.title: Provider and database
settings.config.provider.label: Provider
settings.config.provider.hint: Automatic uses the local database, else ipapi.co unless lookup failures are set to reject. Local database keeps lookups on this server. ipapi.co sends IP addresses to that service. Off turns lookups off.
settings.config.database.statusError: The database status could not be loaded.
settings.config.database.credentials.env: Environment variables are set and take precedence; stored values are ignored.
settings.config.database.accountId.hint: Up to 64 characters. Environment variables take precedence.
settings.config.database.licenseKey.hint: Up to 256 characters. The key is masked and never shown again after saving.
settings.config.database.remove.title: Remove stored MaxMind credentials?
settings.config.database.remove.body: Updates of the GeoIP database stop working unless credentials are set as environment variables.
settings.config.database.saveFirst: Save your changes first, so the download uses the current settings.
settings.config.database.fileName.label: Database file name
settings.config.database.fileName.hint: File name only, inside the plugin's GeoIP folder. Leave empty for the default.
settings.config.alerts.intro: Alerts are sent only when location data is available for the sign-in.
settings.config.alerts.lookupOff: IP location lookup is off, so no alerts are sent.
settings.config.email.title: Security emails to users
settings.config.email.intro: Sent to the end user's own email address, not to administrators.
settings.config.email.enable.label: Send security emails
settings.config.email.types.label: Send an email for
settings.config.email.suspicious.label: Suspicious sign-in
settings.config.email.suspicious.hint: VPN, proxy or threat address, or a score below 70 with scoring on.
settings.config.email.newCountry.label: Sign-in from a new country
settings.config.email.newCountry.hint: The country differs from all of the user's last 50 sessions. Needs at least one earlier country.
settings.config.email.vpnProxy.label: VPN or proxy
settings.config.email.vpnProxy.hint: Needs ipapi.co data; the local database does not detect VPNs or proxies.
settings.config.email.templates.label: Edit email templates
settings.config.email.templates.warning: As soon as any template has content, only your stored templates are used and empty ones are sent empty. Fill in all three, or none.
settings.config.webhooks.title: Team notifications (webhooks)
settings.config.webhooks.intro: Posts every sign-in to Discord or Slack as 'suspicious', 'new country' or 'success'.
settings.config.webhooks.enable.label: Send team notifications
settings.config.webhooks.discord.label: Discord webhook URL
settings.config.webhooks.discord.hint: Must start with https://discord.com or https://discordapp.com. Anyone with this URL can post to your channel.
settings.config.webhooks.slack.label: Slack webhook URL
settings.config.webhooks.slack.hint: Must start with https://hooks.slack.com. Anyone with this URL can post to your channel.
settings.config.retention.intro: Ended sessions stay in the history until they are deleted. The tokens of deleted sessions stay revoked.
settings.config.retention.title: History retention
settings.config.retention.keep.label: Keep ended sessions for
settings.config.retention.keep.hint: Checked once a day, the first time about 24 hours after the server starts. Open sessions are never deleted by retention. 'Forever' keeps them.
settings.config.deleteEnded.title: Delete ended sessions
settings.config.deleteEnded.description: Deletes the records of all ended sessions of all users now. Open sessions, including idle ones, stay.
settings.config.deleteEnded.confirmBody: The records of every ended session of every user are removed permanently from history, statistics and exports. Open sessions, including idle ones, are not affected. This cannot be undone.
